decisions.text:
Here are the direct Celan wording fixes:
1. Sentences needing morl (under / beneath)
"The sharp grain rests by the water under the light."
Old Celan: Pelvar nor dren thal shal.
Updated Celan: Pelvar nor dren morl shal.
"The storm flows with the water under the light."
Old Celan: Dralorim nor dren thal shal.
Updated Celan: Dralorim nor dren morl shal.
"The trap is beneath the bridge."
Old Celan: rinaen vethbel thal njor.
Updated Celan: rinaen vethbel morl njor.
"The cousin is by the water under the mountain."
Old Celan: Pralin ser dren thal morl.
Updated Celan: Pralin ser dren morl morl.
"The distant relative is by the water under the family."
Old Celan: Zharin ser dren thal Tharvok.
Updated Celan: Zharin ser dren morl Tharvok.
"The bond renewal flows under the mountain."
Old Celan: Zhivokesh shalil thal morl.
Updated Celan: Zhivokesh shalil morl morl.
2. Sentence needing vethvar (behind)
"I hear music behind the house."
Old Celan: aenaen I aennor thal teremil.
Updated Celan: aenaen I aennor vethvar teremil.
3. Sentences needing an thal (in/under balance)
"The shadowlight ritual strengthens with the family under balance."
Old Celan: Shalorveth kal dren thal Tharvok.
Updated Celan: Shalorveth kal dren an thal.
"The fortress bonding ceremony is with the family under balance."
Old Celan: Kalorinath ser dren thal Tharvok.
Updated Celan: Kalorinath ser dren an thal.

decisions.text:
Both word order patterns are grammatically valid in Celan, representing two distinct ways the language handles multi-verb actions:
Pattern 1: Interposed Subject (V1 + Subject + V2 + Object)
Example: siv I pralaen krezor.
Translation: "I try to make the hearth."
Syntax Breakdown: [V1: siv] + [Subject: I] + [V2: pralaen] + [Object: krezor]
How it works: This pattern strictly adheres to individual VSO clause mechanics. The subject (I) immediately follows the primary/governing verb (siv = try), placing the secondary action (pralaen = to make) as a complement following the subject.
Pattern 2: Verbal Complex Cluster (V1 + V2 + Subject + Object)
Examples:
siv gavaen I zor. ("I try to hunt the animal.")
sivrethaen belnoraen rakumek nor mekreth. ("The computers fail to synchronize during the system malfunction.")
Syntax Breakdown: [V1 + V2 Cluster: siv gavaen / sivrethaen belnoraen] + [Subject: I / rakumek] + [Object/Modifier]
How it works: In this pattern, the auxiliary verb (siv / sivrethaen) and the main action verb (gavaen / belnoraen) fuse into a compound action cluster at the very front of the sentence. Because Celan prioritizes placing the entire action before the actor, the combined action ("try-to-hunt" or "fail-to-synchronize") is stated first, and the subject follows the full verb cluster.
Recommendation for the App Entry
To ensure learners understand both constructions, the app should document both as permitted strategies:
Strict VSO / Complement Order (V1 + S + V2 + O): Emphasizes the subject's immediate relation to the governing modal verb ("I am trying... to make a hearth").
Action-Cluster Order (V1 + V2 + S + O): Emphasizes the unified compound action arriving before the subject ("The trying-to-hunt is done by me"), aligning with Celan's core action-first philosophy

Correct the extraction rule; keep the definition and only show genuine examples. Elan as an official discourse particle with its proper definition:
Headword: Elan (/eh-lahn/)
Part of Speech: Particle
Meaning: Well… (conversational starter/filler, declarative; typically sentence-initial)

English: "Well, I am going to the water."

decisions.text:
Supply reviewed translations, or clearly label them as untranslated examples. 1. PE-V1-0033: Tha-var La thal Terra.
Reviewed Translation: "They went from the Earth." (or "He/she went out of the living world.") [5, 9, 14]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Tha-var — went (past tense verb: prefix Tha- + verb root Var) [9, 14]
La — he / she / they (3rd person singular neutral pronoun) [9, 14]
thal — from / out of (preposition of origin) [9, 14]
Terra — Earth / Living World (noun) [9, 14]
2. PE-V1-0034: Var I ka shal.
Reviewed Translation: "I go without light." [9]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Var — go / move (verb root) [9, 14]
I — I / me (1st person singular pronoun) [9, 14]
ka — without (preposition) [9, 14]
shal — light (noun) [9, 14]
3. PE-V1-0035: Varan I an Varthas.
Reviewed Translation: "I am in the city." (or "I am residing in / traveling to the city.") [9]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Varan — going / residing (progressive verb: Var + continuous suffix -an) [9, 14]
I — I / me (1st person singular pronoun) [9, 14]
an — at / in (preposition marking physical location) [9, 14]
Varthas — city / town (noun) [9, 14]
4. PE-V1-0036: Nor-var I nor Varthas.
Reviewed Translation: "I will go at the appointed time in the city." [9]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Nor-var — will go (future tense verb: prefix Nor- + verb root Var) [9, 14]
I — I / me (1st person singular pronoun) [9, 14]
nor — at / in (preposition marking temporal setting/time) [9, 14]
Varthas — city / town (noun) [9, 14]
5. PE-V1-0037: Var I esh dren.
Reviewed Translation: "I go above the water." [5, 7, 9]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Var — go / move (verb root) [9, 14]
I — I / me (1st person singular pronoun) [9, 14]
esh — above / over (spatial preposition) [9, 14]
dren — water (noun) [9, 14]
6. PE-V1-0038: Var I morl dren.
Reviewed Translation: "I go under the water." [5, 7, 9]
Grammatical Breakdown:
Var — go / move (verb root) [9, 14]
I — I / me (1st person singular pronoun) [9, 14]
morl — under / beneath (spatial preposition) [9, 14]
dren — water (noun) [9, 14]
